What do each of the variables represent in this formula?
Given on equation sheet
v2 = u2 + 2as
back:
• v — final speed (m/s)
  • u — initial speed (m/s)
  • a — acceleration (m/s2)
  • s — distance moved (m)

front: State the formula for energy transferred (in a circuit)
back:
Learn for exam
energy transferred (J) = charge (C) × voltage (V)
E = Q × V

front: State the equation for average speed
back:
Learn for exam
average speed (m/s) = distance moved (m)time taken (s)
v = st

front: State the formula for acceleration
back:
Learn for exam
acceleration (m/s2) = change in velocity (m/s)time taken (s)
a = v − ut

front: State the formula for force (Newton's second law)
back:
Learn for exam
force (N) = mass (kg) × acceleration (m/s2)
F = m × a

front: State the formula for stopping distance
back:
Learn for exam
stopping distance = thinking distance + braking distance

front: State the formula for electrical power
back:
Learn for exam
power (W) = current (A) × voltage (V)
P = I × V

front: State the formula for voltage (potential difference)
back:
Learn for exam
voltage (V) = current (A) × resistance (Ω)
V = I × R

front: State the formula for charge transferred
back:
Learn for exam
charge (C) = current (A) × time (s)
Q = I × t

front: State the formula for wave speed
back:
Learn for exam
wave speed (m/s) = frequency (Hz) × wavelength (m)
v = f × λ

front: State the formula for refractive index
back:
Learn for exam
n = sin isin r
  • n — refractive index (no unit)
  • i — angle of incidence (°)
  • r — angle of refraction (°)

front: State the formula for critical angle
back:
Learn for exam
sin c = 1n
  • c — critical angle (°)
  • n — refractive index (no unit)

front: State the formula for efficiency
back:
Learn for exam
efficiency (%) = useful energy output (J)total energy output (J) × 100%

front: State the formula for work done
back:
Learn for exam
work done (J) = force (N) × distance moved (m)
W = F × d

front: State the formula for gravitational potential energy
back:
Learn for exam
GPE (J) = mass (kg) × gravitational field strength (N/kg) × height (m)
GPE = m × g × h

front: State the formula for kinetic energy
back:
Learn for exam
kinetic energy (J) = 12 × mass (kg) × speed2 (m/s)
KE = 12 mv2

front: State the formula for density
back:
Learn for exam
density (kg/m3) = mass (kg)volume (m3)
ρ = mV

front: State the formula for pressure
back:
Learn for exam
pressure (Pa) = force (N)area (m2)
p = FA

front: State the formula for pressure difference in a fluid (liquid or gas)
back:
Learn for exam
pressure difference (Pa) = height (m) × density (kg/m3) × gravitational field strength (N/kg)
p = h × ρ × g

front: State the formula for weight
back:
Learn for exam
weight (N) = mass (kg) × gravitational field strength (N/kg)
W = m × g
